correctness.rationale: The cut facet is the product of two simplices, and every polytope face normal cone is described by the complete 2n+1 facet-normal list in the saturated cocharacter lattice. The only positive-dimensional singular orbits correspond to singleton-factor faces of the new facet; their maximal faces give exactly r+s toric irreducible projective components. Old vertices outside the cut facet are isolated singular orbit closures. Explicit dual-lattice semigroup generators and 2x2-minor relations yield the rank-one matrix cone models and their degrees. All nonsimplicial/smooth boundaries are addressed for r,s>=3. Independent exact arithmetic enumerated faces and Smith normal forms for n=6,7,8; this corroborates, but does not prove, the infinite theorem. No false inference from finite tests is used.

value.rationale: For the canonical one-basis deletion of a uniform matroid, the theorem gives the complete reduced singular locus as projective-space strata with K_{r,s} incidence plus isolated higher determinantal points, and computes codimensions and generic multiplicities for an all-parameter family. These local and incidence invariants are not mere rephrasings of the f-vector, require integral normal-cone analysis, and are useful for analyzing toric singularities, Q-factoriality and resolutions. Nongeneric local germs and nonreduced scheme structures remain explicitly outside scope.
